jobs.title: Partnerships Operations Manager
jobs.description:
DOCTRONIC | PARTNERSHIPS


PARTNERSHIPS OPERATIONS MANAGER

New York City, NY • Reports to SVP of Partnerships

 
 


ABOUT DOCTRONIC

Doctronic is the first AI legally authorized to practice medicine. We are processing millions of consultations monthly with 99%+ treatment plan accuracy validated by board-certified clinicians. As our partnership portfolio grows, we're building the operational backbone to make sure every deal we sign is a deal we deliver on.



ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for a Partnerships Operations Manager to serve as a key organizational player on our post-sales partnerships team. Your job is simple to state and hard to do well: make sure our signed partnerships succeed. That means keeping partners, internal stakeholders, and cross-functional teams aligned, organized, and moving toward the deliverables we promised. You'll sit in the room where decisions get made, form your own point of view, and be trusted to keep everyone on track, from deal kickoff through ongoing customer success.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

Partner & Stakeholder Management

 - Serve as a day-to-day point of contact for external partners, building relationships that make Doctronic easy and reliable to work with

 - Manage key internal and external stakeholders, keeping expectations clear on both sides

 - Prepare materials, decks, and briefings that represent Doctronic well in front of partners

 - Attend partner and internal meetings, contribute a real point of view, and drive outcomes rather than just take notes



Cross-Functional Coordination

 - Coordinate with clinical, marketing, operations, finance, and product/engineering to ensure we deliver on every commitment made to a partner

 - Track deliverables across teams and flag risks to timelines before they become problems

 - Act as the connective tissue between partnership commitments and the teams responsible for executing them



Program & Project Infrastructure

 - Build and maintain the systems that keep partnerships organized: kanban and Linear boards, shared Slack channels, and Figma files

 - Own the operational cadence for each partnership: standups, syncs, and follow-through on action items

 - Bring structure to ambiguity, favoring durable systems over one-off fixes



Customer Success & Reporting

 - Own post-launch customer success for partnerships, including recurring partner success meetings

 - Build and send consistent, accurate metrics reporting to partners on an ongoing basis

 - Monitor partner health after launch and escalate early when a relationship needs attention
   
   


WHO YOU ARE

 - 5-7 years of professional experience, ideally spanning partnerships, business operations, program management, or account/customer success in a startup or high-growth environment

 - A proven track record managing complex, multi-stakeholder relationships both internally and externally

 - Highly organized and process-minded: you build systems, not workarounds

 - A clear, confident communicator who can hold their own in a room with partners and executives

 - Comfortable owning a wide scope of work independently, with a bias toward action

 - Fluent with organizational and collaboration tools (Linear, kanban boards, Slack, Figma, or similar)

 - Detail-oriented, with high standards for follow-through on deliverables and metrics

 - Comfortable navigating ambiguity and building structure in a fast-moving environment

 - Healthcare, health tech, or digital health experience is a plus, but not required
   
   


COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

 - $125k-$175k base salary + equity

 - Hybrid role in New York City, working directly alongside our SVP of Partnerships

 - The chance to build the operational infrastructure behind Doctronic's partnerships as we scale

 - Parental Leave: 12 weeks fully paid parental leave for all parents, regardless of gender or path to parenthood — no distinction between birthing and non-birthing parents



Reports to: SVP of Partnerships Location: New York City | Hybrid

jobs.title: FP&A Manager
jobs.description:
Doctronic | Financial Planning & Analysis

 

FP&A Manager

New York City, NY • On-site • Reports to Director of Finance

 

About Doctronic

Doctronic is the first AI legally authorized to practice medicine. We are processing millions of consultations monthly with 99%+ treatment plan accuracy validated by board-certified clinicians. As we scale through our next growth phase, we are building the operational infrastructure to match our ambitions.

About the Role

We are looking for a FP&A Manager to sit at the intersection of FP&A and business operations. This is a high-ownership, hands-on role supporting the Director of Finance across financial controls, vendor management, corporate administration, and compliance operations. You will build and run the systems that keep Doctronic financially disciplined and operationally tight as we grow.

 

What You’ll Do

Financial Planning & Controls

 - Maintain an ongoing, dynamic budget review process - not a static 12-month cycle - so leadership always has a current picture of where we stand

 - Prepare and maintain budget vs. actuals reporting, driving alignment and accountability with senior management

 - Understand and report on weekly cash position to ensure accurate, timely visibility into cash
   
    

Ramp & AP Management

 - Own the end-to-end Ramp workflow from draft invoice ingestion through approval-ready bill preparation

 - Identify and implement process improvements that reduce manual work and accelerate the AP cycle

 - Ensure invoices are clean, coded, and routed correctly before hitting the approval queue

 

Vendor Management

 - Develop and maintain a procurement process that defines who can authorize spend at various thresholds

 - Manage vendor renewal calendars and ensure no material contracts auto-renew without review

 - Build cost models capturing fixed vs. variable costs, contract terms, and payment structure (upfront vs. installment)

 - Coordinate with legal counsel on vendor and consultant contracts as needed

 

Corporate Administration

 - Support the R&D tax credit process by gathering and organizing relevant data and documentation

 - Collect and maintain financial and operational data needed for reporting or compliance such as investor reporting, tax filing, etc.

 - Complete corporate forms and filings (e.g., new banking relationships or payment processor changes)

 - Assist HR on corporate administration tasks such as address changes and entity-level updates

 

Insurance Management

 - Own all business insurance applications, renewals, and policy management

 - Manage insurance requirements specific to healthcare operations, including MSO/PC structure coverage

 - Coordinate with brokers and carriers to ensure adequate and cost-effective coverage at all times
   
    

Who You Are

 - 3–5 years of experience in finance, operations, or a finance-adjacent role - ideally at a startup or high-growth company

 - 2 years of investment banking experience at a top financial institution or comparably rigorous program

 - Highly organized and process-minded: you build systems, not workarounds

 - Comfortable owning a wide scope of work independently, with a bias toward action

 - Detail-oriented with high standards for accuracy, especially in financial reporting and contracts

 - Strong communicator who can work cross-functionally with legal, HR, and senior leadership

 - Proficient with financial tools and platforms; familiarity with Ramp, QuickBooks, or similar systems is a plus

 - Comfortable navigating ambiguity and building structure in a fast-moving environment

Compensation & Benefits

 - Competitive base salary + equity

 - On-site in New York City, working directly alongside executive leadership

 - The chance to build financial and operational infrastructure at a company transforming healthcare with AI

 - Health benefits reimbursement 

 - Flexible PTO

 - Parental Leave: 12 weeks fully paid parental leave for all parents, regardless of gender or path to parenthood — no distinction between birthing and non-birthing parents

 

Reports to: Director of Finance

Location: New York City | On-site

jobs.title: Sales Operations Manager
jobs.description:
ABOUT DOCTRONIC


Doctronic is the #1 AI doctor. Our AI is free, anonymous and HIPAA-compliant, and it has delivered over 30 million consults to date. In December 2025 we became the first and only AI legally authorized to practice medicine, renewing prescriptions autonomously under Utah's AI Learning Lab, and the first AI ever granted medical malpractice insurance. We are live in all 50 states and DC with AI and human physicians available 24/7, and we have raised $65M through our Series B from Abstract, Lightspeed, Union Square Ventures and others.

We are now building the enterprise organization that takes this to health plans, health systems and the wider healthcare ecosystem. This role is the operational backbone of that team.



THE ROLE

Your job is to take everything off our sellers that is not selling.

Right now our enterprise deals slow down in the same place every time: contracting. Diligence questionnaires, security reviews, statements of work, redlines and procurement follow-through all land on people whose time is better spent in front of partners. You will own that layer, and the single number you are graded on is days in contracting, trending down.

You will be the first dedicated operations hire on the enterprise team, reporting to the Chief Business Officer. There is no playbook to inherit, which is the appeal of the job if it is the right job for you.



WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the CRM as the single source of truth: stage definitions, exit criteria, hygiene, and the dashboards leadership actually looks at

 - Run the deal desk: pricing approval routing, statement of work drafting, SLA templates, and redline tracking across concurrent deals

 - Own diligence questionnaires and security questionnaires end to end, coordinating answers from security, compliance, clinical and engineering so a seller never has to chase them

 - Drive procurement and legal follow-through on both sides, and escalate the moment a deal goes quiet

 - Build and run the weekly pipeline review and the monthly board pipeline pack

 - Own forecast hygiene and report on forecast accuracy, so that the number leadership commits to is a number we can trust

 - Build the deal record that implementation and customer success inherit at signature, covering scope, pricing and service commitments

 - Automate what repeats. We would rather you build the process once than run it forty times
   


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 4 to 7 years in sales operations, revenue operations, deal desk or business operations at a B2B company with real enterprise deals

 - Fluent in a modern CRM and comfortable owning configuration yourself rather than filing tickets for it

 - Has personally run diligence or security questionnaire responses, or managed complex enterprise procurement to close

 - Strong analytical skills. Excellent with spreadsheets, comfortable writing SQL or learning to

 - Unusually organized, and a clear writer. Much of this job is making a document say exactly what it needs to say

 - Comfortable being the only operations person, with high autonomy and minimal specs

 - Based in New York City or willing to relocate. This is a hybrid role
   


NICE TO HAVE

 - Enterprise sales operations in healthcare or another regulated industry, where BAAs, DUAs and security review are part of every deal

 - Experience with CPQ or contract lifecycle management tooling

 - Experience with BI tooling and building reporting off a warehouse rather than by hand

 - Has stood up a deal desk or a partner reporting function from scratch

 - Exposure to implementation or post-sales, so you understand what your deal record has to carry downstream
   


COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

 - Base salary range: $125-$150k + equity

 - Health reimbursement allowance, support for well-being, and flexible time off
